source.title: Representation Topology Divergence: A Method for Comparing Neural Network Representations
source.authors: S. Barannikov; I. Trofimov; Nikita Balabin; Evgeny Burnaev

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares representation-similarity measures and reports that their results differ across synthetic point-cloud and UMAP experiments, bearing on metric dependence (V6). It does not test convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures representation differences, but does not sweep model size or capability, test cross-modal alignment, or test whether features or subspaces recur. Training dynamics, data shifts, and other neural-network experiments do not establish the scale trend in the claim. The reported comparison of measures on synthetic clouds and UMAP representations is relevant to V6.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a new similarity measure (RTD) and validates it against CKA, IMD and SVCCA. Its experiments use synthetic point clouds, UMAP embeddings, and comparisons across epochs, layers, distribution shifts, ensembles and transfer learning. None measures whether independently trained models converge, or whether measured convergence between models depends on the metric. The metric-disagreement results concern how well each metric detects known topological changes in synthetic or UMAP data, not convergence between models, so they do not bear on V6 as worded. Convergent Learning (Li et al.) is only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors also state that RTD outperforms CKA, IMD and SVCCA. They stress that its strong correlation with prediction disagreement is a topic for further research.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces RTD, a topological measure, rather than reproducing a scale- or cross-model-convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported metric comparisons vary across point-cloud structures and measures; the MNIST UMAP comparison varies the number of neighbors (10, 20, 50, 100, 200).

fits_no_version.finding: Similarity metrics disagree sharply on known topological changes. On synthetic clusters, Kendall tau is RTD 1.0, CKA 0.23, IMD 0.43 and SVCCA 0.14. On rings, it is RTD 0.8, CKA -0.2, IMD 0.8 and SVCCA -0.2. CKA gives inconsistent orderings of UMAP embeddings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation similarity metrics differ in their sensitivity to topological structure, so conclusions drawn from any one metric may not transfer to others.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-20 ensemble members trained from different random seeds, mean pairwise 1−CKA is 0.094 and RTD is 15.27. Fast Geometric Ensemble members score 0.033 and 10.45. The relative difference between ensemble types is 64.9% for CKA versus 31.6% for RTD (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How dissimilar different-seed networks appear depends on the metric. No baseline is given that would show feature convergence.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML); Proceedings of the 39th ICML, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: The results relevant to metric dependence are limited to selected synthetic point-cloud experiments and MNIST UMAP representations. The study does not test model scaling, cross-modal alignment, or convergence as capability increases.
record.rows_left_out: Other neural-network experiments, including training dynamics, distribution shifts, transfer learning, and ensembles, do not test convergence with model scale. The paper also refers to results in figures without giving numerical values in the text; those values were not inferred.

untested.parts: Alignment of models with different architectures, objectives and data as scale or capability grows.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds. The ensemble distances do not test feature or subspace overlap.
Mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
Whether measured convergence between models changes with the metric, its settings or the inputs. The metric comparisons use synthetic and UMAP data only.
Plateau or incompleteness of alignment, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.

record.verdict_notes: This is a measure-proposal paper. All extracted rows benchmark the authors' own method against rival metrics on synthetic or UMAP data. None bears on any version, so no verdicts are given and the reader's V6 'supports' labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: Whether representations of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data become more aligned as models grow and become more capable.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions as both models improve.
Whether different initializations learn common features or shared subspaces; ensemble-member representation distances do not test feature or subspace overlap.
Mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The paper tests differences among selected similarity measures and representation settings, but does not systematically vary RTD's settings or test out-of-distribution robustness.
Whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.
